listening_script.speed_note: Read aloud at a normal, clear pace (85 wpm). Pause 2–3 seconds between sentences. Read the full text twice before students answer questions.
listening_script.text:
Electricity is the flow of tiny particles called ELECTRONS.
HOW ELECTRICITY WORKS:
1. CIRCUIT
- A path for electricity to flow
- Needs: power source, wires, load (like a light bulb)
- Must be a complete loop!
2. CONDUCTORS
- Materials that let electricity flow through
- Examples: metals (copper, aluminum, gold)
3. INSULATORS
- Materials that DON'T let electricity flow
- Examples: rubber, plastic, wood
TYPES OF ELECTRICITY:
1. STATIC ELECTRICITY
- Electricity that stays in one place
- Example: rubbing a balloon on your hair
2. CURRENT ELECTRICITY
- Electricity that flows
- What powers our homes and devices
ELECTRICITY SAFETY:
- Never touch electrical outlets with wet hands
- Don't put metal objects in outlets
- Stay away from power lines
- Unplug devices before cleaning them
Electricity is useful but can be dangerous!
WEEKS 93-96: GOVERNMENT & ECONOMICS
